messages:
incident-bot: PAGED SRE - HIGH severity
incident-bot: service=inference-api region=us-east-1 symptom=429+503_spike 429_5m=18% 503_5m=4% runbook=/runbooks/inference-rate-errors

Maya Patel: seeing 429s plateauing ~18% for the last 6 minutes, mostly on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/d/INFERENCE/429-503-overview

Elena Zhao: confirmed - origin looks to be a mix of bursty public traffic + a few keys sending very high concurrent requests. Top offender API keys: api_key_3, api_key_12, api_key_81 (anonymized).

Carlos Diaz: 503s are coming from model-worker pool in us-east-1, logs show repeated `worker oom` and `request timeout` on gpu-node-7. Suspect backend saturation.

Maya Patel: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) tighten per-key rate limits for unverified/free keys, 2) route high-concurrency keys to lower-cost fallback model, 3) temporarily disable streaming on non-enterprise keys to reduce socket pressure. Thoughts?

Rohit Singh: +1 for per-key throttles. I'll push a quick rate-limit patch to the edge-proxy config and bump quota enforcement.

Elena Zhao: I'll open canaries to divert 20% of traffic to redwood-small for non-enterprise keys to reduce GPU load on big models.

Carlos Diaz: while you do that, I'll restart the model-worker processes on gpu-node-7 and raise the worker count by 1 on the autoscaler to catch up. Running `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-worker -n inference --context=us-east-1` now.

Maya Patel: Customer impact: CS dashboard shows ~3 customers with >50% error rates (IDs: cust-501, cust-728, cust-912). Reached out to CS for heads-up.

CustomerSuccessBot: Notified customer success team: 3 customers flagged (cust-501, cust-728, cust-912). Assigned to Elena for ETA comms.

Rohit Singh: Pushing rate-limit change via control-plane API. Patch applied: `edge.rate_limits.free_tier=5rps`, `edge.concurrent_limit.free_tier=2`

Rohit Singh: admin API call:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/edge/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"rate_limits":{"free_tier":{"rps":5,"concurrent":2}}}'
```

Maya Patel: Also enabling feature-flag to disable streaming for non-enterprise keys: `feature.streaming_reduced=false` -> set to `true` for gating.

Elena Zhao: Canaries to redwood-small kicking in. Initial numbers: 429 down to 9% in the canary buckets, overall 429 now 11% (5m). Still seeing 503 bursts ~3-4%.

Carlos Diaz: Restart helped but worker errors still show occasional OOMs. Adding `--max-batch-tokens=1024` to model-worker to reduce memory footprint. Applying via helm: `helm upgrade --reuse-values inference -f worker-overrides.yaml`

Maya Patel: Noted. Also temporarily increasing quota for enterprise keys cust-728 to avoid SLO violations for paying customers: bumped `cust-728.concurrency=20` for 30m.

Rohit Singh: I'm seeing tail latencies improving. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/d/INFERENCE/live-mitigation?orgId=1&panelId=7

Elena Zhao: 429 trend is at 6.5% over last 5m. 503s falling to 1.2% but still spikey during deployments.

Maya Patel: Quick note for post-incident: record exact knobs we toggled (edge rate limits, streaming feature flag, fallback routing, worker batch size), and timeline for rollback.

Rohit Singh: I'm taking the on-call handoff. My shift covers until 04:00 UTC. I'll keep monitoring the dashboards and the incident channel. If anything regresses to >10% 429 or >2% 503 for 10m, page me.

Maya Patel: Thanks, Rohit — leaving now. I filed the initial incident ticket INC-2026-145 (brief) with mitigation steps.

Carlos Diaz: I'll keep a watch on node OOMs and follow-up with infra for possible kernel/memory tuning on gpu-node-7.

Elena Zhao: I'll keep canaries running and prepare a rollout plan to permanently divert low-quality traffic to smaller models if this pattern repeats.

Rohit Singh: Current summary (at handoff): 429 reduced from 18% -> 6.5%, 503 from 4% -> 1.2%. Mitigations in place: tightened free-tier rate limits, disabled streaming for non-enterprise, canary fallback to redwood-small, worker restart and batch-size reduction, temporary enterprise quota bump. Escalation: if 429 >10% for 10m or 503 >3% for 5m, escalate to oncall lead and consider capacity-scale in us-east-1.

Maya Patel: +1 on escalation thresholds. Please update incident channel with final postmortem link once done.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-145 updated: status=monitoring owner=Rohit Singh severity=high

Rohit Singh: I'll post a short blameless timeline and action items later today. Taking over now.
